s: One had an eye drawn down and was called Uk-kwûnagi'ta, "Eye-drawn-down."
The other had an arm twisted out of shape and was called Uk-ku'sûñtsûti, "Bent-bow-shape."
They killed a deer and cooked the meat in a pot.
The second old man dipped a piece of bread into the soup and smacked his lips as he ate it.
"Is it good?" said the first old man.
It will draw down one's eye."
Thought the first old man to himself, "He means me."
So he dipped a piece of bread into the pot, and smacked his lips as he tasted it.
"Do you find it good?" said the other old man.
It will twist up one's arm."
Thought the second old man, "He means me"; so he got very angry and struck the first old man, and then they fought until each killed the other.
